standard_prerequisites.name: The specialization relation between points and the meaning of the phrases specializations lift and generalizations lift along a continuous map
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's section on specialization, immediately before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the two properties whose composition-stability the statement asserts.

core_obligations: Start with a specialization in the target of the composite: the proof takes a specialization z-prime leading to z and a point of the source mapping to z-prime (proof lines 3855-3856).
Lift along the second map: the lifting hypothesis for the map on the target produces a point of the middle space above z, specializing from the image of the chosen point (proof lines 3856-3857).

Lift along the first map: the lifting hypothesis for the first map then produces a specialization in the source starting at the chosen point and mapping onto the lifted point, which is exactly what lifting along the composite requires (proof lines 3858-3861).
The other case: the author states that the argument for generalizations is the same (proof line 3861).
proof_roadmap: 取 Z 中的 specialization z' ⇝ z 以及 X 中映到 z' 的点 x'。
先用 g 的提升性得到 f(x') ⇝ y 且 g(y) = z，再用 f 的提升性得到 x' ⇝ x 且 f(x) = y；于是 specialization 沿 g∘f 提升。generalizations 情形相同。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the composition-stability of the two lifting properties (author lemma at source lines 3846-3852, label lemma-lift-specialization-composition): if specializations lift along both maps of a composable pair then they lift along the composite, and likewise for generalizations. The proof (source lines 3854-3862) is a two-step diagram chase that uses each lifting hypothesis once, in the correct order (proof lines 3855-3861), and the author notes that the other case is the same. The lemma is what makes the chapter's later statements about lifting along towers of maps meaningful. H2.
